newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Samper denies calling all Colombians criminals.
newsitem.headline: Samper denies calling all Colombians criminals.

text.p: Embattled President Ernesto Samper has denied suggesting that all Colombians are criminals because they all share links to the drug trade.

In a statement issued on Thursday night, Samper's spokesman said his remarks in an interview with CNN last week in New York, where he addressed the United Nations General Assembly, had been taken out of context and twisted around in an "absurd" way.
Samper himself has been has been dogged by charges that he financed his 1994 election campaign with drug dollars.
Samper's spokesman demanded a retraction from CNN, saying Samper's comments had been edited to make it sound like he was scorning his countrymen instead of defending them.
In the interview, which prompted a public outcry in Colombia, Samper was quoted as saying "there's not a single person in Colombia who isn't associated directly or indirectly with drug trafficking."
According to a text of the interview released by the presidential palace, Samper was merely paraphrasing his interviewer's question, however.
Samper, who went on to say in the interview that the unsavory drug-tainted image Colombians suffer around the globe was undeserved and the result of an unfair sterotype.
"The linking of Colombia and all Colombians to drug trafficking is the result, exactly, of the unfair treatment of Colombians abroad," he said.
